label: copy-phase input 0 (esp. first copy step after <DEL>), rare
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.008% of steps), firing only in the copy phase and always on a repeated input (in_first=0). 81% of mass is on copy-phase input 0, 15% on input c. 81% of mass is at recall_idx=1, the step just after <DEL> where the fed-back input is the first original token, so first_tok=0 has 19x lift. The strongest activations are on sequences that start 0 z..., where the step outputs z (out_tok=z, 23x lift); next_out=z/3 is also enriched. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Precision is very low: input 0 in the copy phase is true on ~91k dev steps, but the feature fires on only 542. Requiring recall_idx=1, input 0, and output z raises precision to 0.23 but drops recall to 0.24. So it is gated by some extra sequence context that I could not capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=c (+4.02), next_out=z (+3.84), phase=2 & in_tok=0 (+3.68), phase=2 & out_tok=z (+3.10), phase=2 & out_tok=c (+3.08), in_tok=0 (+2.95). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.00), recall_idx=3 (-1.74), orig1=0 (-1.59), orig8=- (-1.13).
